cards.prompt: Teachers rate their burnout before and after a summer break. Same teachers, two time points.
cards.explain: Two scores from the same people: test each person's change with a paired t-test.

cards.prompt: Exam scores of students randomly assigned to online or face-to-face sections.
cards.explain: Two separate groups of different people, one numeric outcome.

cards.prompt: Your 35 principals' mean leadership score compared with the national norm of 3.2.
cards.explain: One group against a known value: `t.test(x, mu = 3.2)`.

cards.prompt: Job satisfaction of teachers in rural, suburban and urban schools.
cards.explain: Three groups: one ANOVA instead of three t-tests, which would inflate the false-alarm rate.

cards.prompt: Test anxiety scores against a norm of 28.
Welch's t-test of post-test anxiety by group.
cards.explain: Outcome on the left of `~`, grouping variable on the right.

cards.prompt: Student's version, SPSS's "Equal variances assumed" row.
cards.explain: R defaults to Welch's test; `var.equal = TRUE` gives Student's.
car centres on the median by default (Brown–Forsythe); SPSS centres on the mean.

cards.prompt: The paired t-test of pre- against post-test anxiety.
cards.explain: Without it R runs a two-group test, which gives an answer, just the wrong one for this design.

choices: the difference in means divided by the pooled SD
the difference in means divided by the SE
the t statistic divided by n
cards.explain: A difference in SD units, so it doesn't depend on sample size. Dividing by the SE gives t instead.

cards.prompt: R gives p = 0.0000178. How is it reported in APA style?
cards.explain: Exact values down to .001; anything smaller is *p* < .001.
